exposure: Women who underwent non-obstetric pelvic surgery during pregnancy vs. women who did not undergo surgery
Non-obstetric pelvic surgery during pregnancy (laparoscopy or laparotomy)
cohort: 4,439,778 women who gave birth in Korea between 2006 and 2016
finding: Non-obstetric pelvic surgery during pregnancy was associated with a higher risk of preterm birth, LBW, gestational hypertension, placenta previa, placental abruption, and C/S.
mod_finding: While both laparoscopy and laparotomy during pregnancy were associated with adverse outcomes, laparoscopic adnexal mass resection was associated with a lower risk of LBW compared to laparotomy.
